issues.legal_issue: Evidence from a related witness and from witnesses declared hostile may be relied on to establish an accused’s participation when the dependable parts of their testimony are corroborated by other evidence.
material_facts: A brother of the deceased testified that all three accused were present and attacked the deceased.

Four labourers were declared hostile, but their testimony supported that two accused were present and confronted the deceased; one labourer also testified that he later saw three persons surrounding the deceased.
Weapons were recovered from the accused, including a cutting weapon from the accused whose presence was disputed.
Medical evidence attributed the death to head injuries and haemorrhage and was consistent with the account of an attack.
issues.conclusion: The relationship of the principal witness to the deceased did not by itself make his evidence unreliable, and the dependable portions of the hostile witnesses’ evidence were not erased from the record. Considered with the recoveries and medical evidence, the evidence established the accused’s participation, including that of the accused whose presence was disputed.
issues.legal_principle: A related witness’s evidence is scrutinized with care as a rule of prudence, not rejected merely because of the relationship; a court may rely on a sole related witness whose testimony is trustworthy and corroborated (Mano Dutt v. State of Uttar Pradesh, relying on Anil Phukan v. State of Assam). A hostile witness’s evidence is not effaced or rejected en bloc; the court may accept the dependable portions after careful scrutiny and ordinarily look for corroboration (Paramjeet Singh alias Pamma v. State of Uttarakhand; State of Rajasthan v. Bhawani; Radha Mohan Singh v. State of U.P.; Mahesh v. State of Maharashtra; Rajendra v. State of U.P.; Govindappa v. State of Karnataka; Mrinal Das v. State of Tripura; Khachar Dipu alias Dilipbhai Nakubhai v. State of Gujarat).

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.related_witness_gave_testimony_about_the: A witness related to the victim testified about the accused’s presence or conduct during the attack.
predicates.hostile_witnesses_supported_material_par: Witnesses declared hostile testified to material circumstances such as the accused’s presence, confrontation with the victim, or surrounding the victim.
predicates.weapon_recovery_connected_accused_to_the: A weapon connected with the attack was recovered from an accused.
predicates.medical_findings_corresponded_to_the_acc: Medical findings were consistent with the account of the attack and its fatal injuries.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction is appealed, testimony by a related witness and dependable portions of hostile witnesses’ testimony, supported by weapon recovery or consistent medical findings, can establish the accused’s participation.

issues.legal_issue: A killing committed in a sudden fight without premeditation, in the heat of passion, and without undue advantage or cruel conduct falls within the sudden-fight exception to murder, while injuries indicating intention and knowledge support conviction for culpable homicide with intention.
material_facts: A dispute over cutting a tree led to a verbal altercation, during which the accused attacked the deceased.
The evidence showed that the attack occurred during the sudden altercation and was not premeditated.
Although the accused had weapons, the sequence of events and the injuries did not show that they took undue advantage or acted cruelly.
The deceased sustained serious injuries to the head, including injuries to multiple regions of the head, which indicated intention and knowledge.
issues.conclusion: The sudden-fight exception applied, so the murder conviction was modified to a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder with intention, rather than a conviction based only on knowledge.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC requires a sudden fight, absence of premeditation, action in the heat of passion, and no undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct; the fight must be with the person killed. The number of wounds is not decisive, and ‘undue advantage’ means unfair advantage (Surinder Kumar v. Union Territory of Chandigarh; Arumugam v. State). Where there is intention and knowledge, the offence falls under Section 304 Part I IPC; where there is knowledge but no intention, it falls under Section 304 Part II IPC.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and sudden_fight_with_the_deceased and no_premeditation and acted_in_heat_of_passion and not undue_advantage_taken and not cruel_or_unusual_conduct and fatal_injuries_indicated_intention_and_knowledge

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.sudden_fight_with_the_deceased: The accused and the person killed engaged in a sudden fight.
predicates.no_premeditation: The attack was not planned in advance.
predicates.acted_in_heat_of_passion: The accused acted while passions were aroused by the sudden confrontation and had no time to cool down.
predicates.undue_advantage_taken: The accused used an unfair advantage during the fight.
predicates.cruel_or_unusual_conduct: The accused acted cruelly or in an unusual manner during the fight.
predicates.fatal_injuries_indicated_intention_and_k: The nature and location of the fatal injuries indicated that the accused acted with intention and knowledge.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a criminal conviction, a sudden unplanned fight in the heat of passion without unfair advantage or cruel conduct, together with fatal injuries indicating intention and knowledge, results in a conviction for culpable homicide with intention rather than murder.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence may be reduced to the period already served after a conviction is modified when the time already spent in custody and the circumstances of the offence warrant that result.
material_facts: The conviction was modified from murder to culpable homicide with intention.
The accused had already spent a substantial period in custody by the time the sentence was reviewed.
The Court took account of the circumstances in which the offence was committed.
issues.conclusion: The sentence was reduced to the period already undergone, and the accused were ordered released unless required in another case.
issues.legal_principle: After modifying the conviction, the Court assessed the sentence in light of the circumstances of the offence and the custody already served; no separate statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this sentencing determination.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and conviction_modified_after_review and substantial_custody_already_served and offence_circumstances_considered

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.conviction_modified_after_review: The reviewing court changed the conviction after considering the case.
predicates.substantial_custody_already_served: The convicted persons had already spent a substantial period in custody.
predicates.offence_circumstances_considered: The court considered the circumstances in which the offence was committed when determining sentence.

issues.definition: When a conviction is modified on appeal, substantial custody already served and consideration of the offence circumstances can result in a sentence limited to the period already served.
